svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.11.1.1 Required Protection
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.11 SOUND TRANSMISSION
Required Protection

g.text: constructions. ASTC counts both, STC the first
material, ii stud spaces filled, iii resilient
channel one side, iv 12.7 mm gypsum board.
Or STC 43 or more (b), or ASTC 40 or more (c)
from an elevator shaft or refuse chute:
STC rates the separating assembly. ASTC
also takes in the flanking transmission paths,
so it is the better indicator of protection

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
A dwelling unit is separated from every other space
in a building in which noise may be generated
By (a) a separating assembly and adjoining
constructions, which together provide an ASTC rating of
not less than 47, or (b) a separating assembly providing
an STC rating of not less than 50 and adjoining
constructions that conform to Article 9.11.1.4. Except
as in Sentences (2) and (3). See Note A-9.11.1.4.
Where a house contains a secondary suite, each
dwelling unit is separated from every other space in
the house in which noise may be transmitted
By (a) construction having (i) joist spaces filled with
sound-absorbing material of not less than 150 mm (5⅞″)
nominal thickness, (ii) stud spaces filled with
sound-absorbing material, (iii) a resilient channel on
one side of the separation spaced 400 or 600 mm o.c.,
and (iv) not less than 12.7 mm (½″) thick gypsum board
on ceilings and on both sides of walls, (b) construction
providing an STC rating of not less than 43, or (c) a
separating assembly and adjoining constructions
providing an ASTC rating of not less than 40. See
Construction separating a dwelling unit from an
elevator shaft or refuse chute has an STC rating of
not less than 55
Drawn: A rooms with near walls cut away, B a floor slice seen from above with the subfloor cut back, C a plan.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.11.1.1. (page 9-103), with Note A-9.11.
